answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, select players + 1 face-down, place them on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; turns proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'number of players + 1'; 'without looking'; '11 marked territories'; 'one structure bonus tile'; 'lowest-numbered Player Mat starts'.

answers.answer: On the map, each player puts their character on their home base, one worker on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it, and four mechs over their abilities on the Faction Mat. The Player Mat supplies six technology cubes, four structures, four recruits, and six remaining workers for Produce's red rectangles. The Faction Mat determines starting power and starting combat-card draw; the Player Mat determines starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards. Six stars start by the faction emblem.
answers.evidence: Setup items 3–4: Faction Mat sets 'starting power and draw starting combat cards'; Player Mat sets 'starting popularity' and 'starting coins and objectives'; map placements and quantities are specified there.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action, either action, or both. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. If taking both, take the top before the bottom and cannot return to the top. Pay all exposed red-box costs before the action; benefits are exposed green boxes. The exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'different section'; 'either, both, or neither'; 'Rusviet may repeat'; 'top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost'; 'First pay the full cost'; amounts vary by mat and upgrades.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities without control except that a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. You may spend resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources'; 'Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities'; costs use resources from 'any territories you currently control'.

answers.answer: On an unupgraded Move, you may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; you cannot move one unit twice. All units can carry any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A worker carried by a mech may subsequently move itself; a worker may also board a mech before its later move.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: 'two different units, one adjacent territory each'; 'cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice'; unit carrying rules and carried-worker movement are stated.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with only enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. The workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; the player loses one popularity per worker, down to zero, so zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move rules: character/mech entering 'enemy workers only' stops; workers retreat; 'Lose one popularity per worker ... down to zero'; a worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Resolve combat after all units finish the Move action and before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order if there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Combat: 'After all units finish a Move action' and 'before any subsequent bottom action'; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Move rules prohibit workers independently moving 'into or out of' enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. A built Monument also gives one popularity. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades; a built Armory also gives one power. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade sections specify costs, choices, building bonuses, exhausted-deck handling, and resource placement/worker restriction.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing, and choose up to two different controlled territories. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right after payment and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: 'must afford all of it'; choose up to 'two different controlled territories'; workers taken 'left to right, after payment'; 'may decline'; new costs affect 'future' actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move a cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: place a mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses. Exact resource quantities and coin amounts are mat-specific and not given in the summary.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions state 'Upgrade — oil', 'Deploy — metal', their placement/effect details, and that completed actions may still be paid for coins and ongoing recruit bonuses; exact costs are on the mat.

answers.answer: Build costs wood and puts a structure from your Player Mat on a controlled territory with your worker. Only one structure total may occupy a territory; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill is an additional Produce territory and produces as one worker only while controlled; it works without an actual worker there. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for all your units, including Factory Move, even when enemy-controlled. The summary does not explicitly describe Mine use when enemy units occupy its territory beyond the Mine remaining your tunnel.
answers.evidence: Build subsection gives cost, placement and permanence; Mill works only 'while controlled'; Mine is a personal tunnel 'including when an enemy controls its territory'.

answers.answer: Enlist costs food. Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and place it permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered at the recruit's former Player Mat position, regardless of the one-time bonus chosen. It triggers when you or either immediate neighbor takes that corresponding bottom-row action, not for top actions, encounters, or similar Factory actions. Resolve active player, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers it once, not twice. The four ongoing bonuses are Upgrade: one power; Deploy: one coin; Build: one popularity; Enlist: one combat card.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections specify food, token placement, four one-time bonuses, source of ongoing bonus, triggers, order, game-end cutoff, two-player rule, and ongoing quantities.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of 7 or current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Both players deduct their dial power from their power track and discard all played cards face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify dial/card limits, Rusviet addition, ability order, totals, attacker winning ties, and payment/discard rules.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally no more than two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). The losing player's characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4–5 lists territory/resource control, star limits, retreating units/resources, popularity loss, and loser card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory: discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs apply and no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters section specifies timing, lost-entry outcome, destination for gains, printed costs, and no normal action costs/mat/recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Every player's character must take a Factory card on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary): look at the available cards, choose one, and return the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. It acts as a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the usual no-repeat rule (except Rusviet). Factory actions provide no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Its bottom action moves one unit up to two territories during that Move action, or a character/mech with Speed up to three; Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section specifies each player's first visit, card choice, no later exchange, action-section use, absent bonuses, and bottom-action movement distances.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal, though you may wait. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony may score both and keeps the second card after the first.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section states turn timing, all-requirements-at-reveal, both-card discard destination, normal limit, and Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent and another player's stars do not block a goal. The sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end section enumerates all achievements, limits, permanence, nonblocking rule, and sixth-star ending.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Neighbor recruit stars happen only after the active player finishes the action and only if no earlier sixth star ended the game. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of the movement by returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end section specifies collection before the star, neighbor bonus timing/cutoff, and undoing unresolved battle movement.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, stars score $4 each, territories $3 each, and every complete pair of controlled resources $2. Five stars score $20; four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories and score $21; 13 resources make six pairs and score $12. Those components total $53, added to held coins and the selected structure bonus. The structure bonus remains eligible even if enemies control your structure territories, but the exact bonus amount is unsupported without the selected tile and qualifying structure/feature counts. Victory ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune gives the 7–12 popularity rates and example of $20 + $21 + $12 = $53; structure bonus says it applies even if enemies control the structures' territories; tie-break order is listed.
